abstract: Expression quantitative trait loci studies have highlighted TSPAN10 as a gene that confers an increased risk of developing age-related macular degeneration (AMD). The mechanism for this and the role of TSPAN10 in retinal cells such as the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and its contribution to AMD pathology are unknown. We report the generation of human embryonic stem cell derived RPE with TSPAN10 knockout using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing. This provided an in vitro model to investigate the functions of TSPAN10. TSPAN10 knockout cells were differentiated into mature RPE. Significant differences were observed in cell pigmentation, polarisation and cell body height, and the response to oxidative stress in comparison to wild type. These results demonstrate for the first time a role for TSPAN10 in the RPE, aligning with published data to support the importance of TSPAN10 for pigmentation, and adding to our understanding of the heterogeneous disease AMD.
